metadata.purpose: Validate Scientific Reflow generalizability to XAS operando measurements at 8-ID ISS

reference_paper.title: Low-iridium stabilized ruthenium oxide anode catalyst for durable proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis

metadata.validation_approach: Model operando electrochemical experiment (Systems A-F), run gap closure, infer catalyst degradation mechanism from time-resolved XAS

validation_strategy.description: We will treat the Ru6IrOx catalyst as having PARTIALLY_KNOWN properties (crystal structure and initial oxidation states known, degradation pathway and operando oxidation state evolution UNKNOWN), then use gap closure to see if we can infer the degradation mechanism from time-resolved XAS measurements.
known_beforehand: Crystal structure: Rutile RuO2 with Ir substitution
discovered_by_experiment: Ru oxidation state evolution during OER
Ir oxidation state evolution during OER
Critical Ir concentration in subsurface layer
Degradation pathway: Ru dissolution vs Ir stabilization
validation_strategy.gap_closure_target: Can we infer the catalyst degradation mechanism (oxidation state changes, dissolution pathway) from operando XAS spectra?
validation_strategy.success_criteria: Gap closure should propose: (1) Ru oxidation state increases under OER conditions, (2) Ir stabilizes Ru by occupying subsurface sites, (3) Degradation occurs via Ru dissolution to soluble Ru^(6+)

physical_interactions.description: Damping wiggler generates broad-spectrum hard X-rays, monochromator selects Ru K-edge (22.1 keV) or Ir L-edge (11.2 keV)

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: X-ray absorption at Ru/Ir edges, core-level excitation
physical_interactions.description: Hard X-rays excite Ru 1s → 4p/continuum (K-edge) or Ir 2p → 5d/continuum (L-edge) transitions

physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Applied potential 0-2 V vs RHE, current density up to 2 A/cm^2
physical_interactions.description: Electrochemical potential drives OER (2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e-), changes catalyst oxidation state

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: X-ray fluorescence (Ru Kα, Ir Lα emission after core-hole decay)
physical_interactions.interaction_strength: Fluorescence yield ~0.5-0.8 for K-edge (Ru), ~0.1-0.3 for L-edge (Ir)

measured_data.ru_k_edge_shift: XANES edge position shifts to higher energy under OER conditions (oxidation)
measured_data.ir_l_edge_stability: XANES edge position remains stable (Ir resists oxidation)
measured_data.time_evolution: Ru edge shifts over time (hours-days), Ir edge stable
measured_data.coordination_changes: EXAFS oscillations show Ru-O distance changes, Ir-Ru bonding
measured_data.degradation_signature: Gradual Ru edge shift → dissolution as Ru^6+?

physical_interactions.description: THIS IS THE CRITICAL DATA - XAS measures time-resolved oxidation state evolution. Ru edge shift encodes degradation pathway.

physical_interactions.physical_mechanism: Asynchronous data stream synchronization and XAS processing
physical_interactions.description: System F processes raw detector signals → μ(E,t) absorption spectra. Enables time-resolved operando analysis.

ru_oxidation_under_oer.interpretation: Ru oxidation state increases at high potential, approaches Ru^6+ dissolution threshold

ir_oxidation_under_oer.interpretation: Ir resists oxidation better than Ru, provides stabilization

degradation_mechanism.description: Ru surface atoms oxidize to Ru^6+ and dissolve into electrolyte
degradation_mechanism.ir_stabilization_role: Ir in subsurface layer prevents Ru dissolution by modifying electronic structure
degradation_mechanism.stability_metric: 1500h at 2 A/cm^2 (80% Ir reduction vs commercial catalysts)

coordination_environment.ir_substitution_effect: Ir-O bonds slightly longer (~2.0 Å), stabilize local structure

measured_observables: Time-resolved XAS μ(E,t) at Ru K-edge shows edge shift (oxidation)
Time-resolved XAS μ(E,t) at Ir L-edge shows stability (no oxidation)
gap_closure_configuration.matrix_formulation: Infer System D (oxidation states, degradation mechanism) from measured D→E interaction (XAS spectra) and C→D interaction (electrochemical conditions) given known A, B, C, E, F
gap_closure_configuration.expected_outcome: Gap closure should propose: (1) Ru oxidizes under OER, (2) Ir stabilizes surface, (3) Degradation via Ru dissolution

success_criteria.ru_oxidation_detected: Gap closure identifies Ru oxidation state increase under OER conditions
success_criteria.ir_stability_detected: Gap closure identifies Ir oxidation state remains stable
success_criteria.degradation_mechanism_inferred: Gap closure proposes Ru dissolution as degradation pathway
success_criteria.ir_stabilization_role_inferred: Gap closure recognizes Ir subsurface stabilization prevents Ru dissolution

comparison_to_published.published_degradation: Ru dissolution to Ru^6+, Ir stabilization via subsurface sites
comparison_to_published.verdict: TBD (PASS if qualitatively correct mechanism inferred)

similarities: System D is PARTIALLY_KNOWN (target of discovery)
Gap closure goal is to infer System D properties
differences: System A: Damping wiggler (hard X-rays) vs EPU49 undulator (soft X-rays)
System C: Operando electrochemical cell (dynamic) vs cryostat (static)
System E: Fluorescence detector (absorption) vs RIXS spectrometer (energy loss)
System F: REQUIRED for ISS (async DAQ), NOT NEEDED for RIXS
Time domain: Time-resolved (1500h) vs single snapshot
comparison_to_rixs_case.key_insight: Systems A-E are generalizable, but System F is CONDITIONALLY REQUIRED (for time-resolved techniques)

notes.validation_approach: This test validates that Scientific Reflow can generalize beyond RIXS to operando XAS. If gap closure successfully infers the degradation mechanism (Ru oxidation → dissolution, Ir stabilization), it confirms the Systems A-F architecture is beamline-agnostic.
notes.system_f_importance: System F (async DAQ) is CRITICAL for operando XAS. Without it, we cannot capture time-resolved oxidation state evolution. This validates the addition of System F to the architecture.
notes.challenge: Operando XAS is more complex than RIXS: (1) time-dependent, (2) electrochemical environment varies, (3) degradation is slow (hours-days). Gap closure must handle time-varying System C→D and D→E interactions.
notes.next_steps: After running this validation, compare with XPCS case (11-ID CHX) to see if all three beamlines confirm Systems A-F generalizability.
